transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alicia Chen (CTO, Lumen), Marcus Lee (ML Eng), Nina Patel (Security), Tom Reeves (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): quick conversation about getting started with redwood, free creeds, time to first token, also at mention of dedicated/private for production.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Alicia: good, thanks. Excited to learn more about your quickstart. We've been looking at a few options for shipping LLM features.
[00:20] Jordan: Great — quick agenda: show the PLG/self-serve experience, what free credits look like, typical time-to-first-token and then high-level when teams move to Dedicated or Private. Priya will cover the technical bits.
[00:32] Priya: hi all, quick note, i'll talk about runtime, latency/cost tradeoffs, and how to run a small benchmark. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:42] Marcus: quick question up front — we prototype in a couple hours usually; how long does your quickstart take to get a token out?
[00:50] Jordan: normally customers can get to first-token in 15-30 minutes with our quickstart — sign up, redeem creds, curl or SDK sample, and run a simple prompt. We'll send the exact curl snippets.
[01:05] Marcus: sweet. And free credits? how big is the trial?
[01:09] Jordan: we provide starter credits (we'll send the current promo) — typically enough for thousand-ish requests, depends on model and prompt length. For early evals it's plenty.
[01:17] Nina: security question — is hosted API SOC2? what about encryption/KMS and SSO?
[01:22] Priya: yes we are SOC2 compliant for hosted; we also support SAML SSO and RBAC. For encryption, hosted supports envelope encryption and integrates with customer KMS for Dedicated and Private. We'll share the SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM integration notes.
[01:38] Nina: and data residency? we have EU customers so need logs to stay in region for some flows.
[01:44] Jordan: we have region routing and can keep data in specific regions on Dedicated/Private — hosted has multiple regions but the Dedicated/private options give stronger controls for residency.
[01:54] Tom: from infra side — if we move to Dedicated, what does capacity look like? and how do you handle autoscaling?
[02:02] Priya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, you get predictable throughput and configurable autoscaling policies + burst capacity. We also have routing policies so you can fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained.
[02:18] Marcus: latency vs cost — curious what typical per-token latencies we should expect for a 1k context rtrn?
[02:26] Priya: it varies by model and hardware but for optimized open models on GPU we aim for single-digit token latencies at steady state for generation; inference engine does continuous batching, KV cache and kernel selection to keep latency low. For longer contexts you may see higher tail latencies. We can benchmark your workload during POC.
[02:44] Jordan: customers often start on hosted for speed to value, then move to Dedicated when they need predictable unit economics or to meet compliance. Private deploy is used when they need VPC/on-prem control and an isolated control plane.
[02:57] Alicia: what's required from our side to start? we have a tiny internal app and want to build a prototype this week.
[03:05] Jordan: sign up, confirm your org, redeem credits — we'll give you an API key scoped to the trial. Use our quickstart repo or SDKs (python/node). Time to first-token tends to be 15-30 minutes including account setup.
[03:20] Marcus: any rate limits for trial?
[03:23] Jordan: trial accounts have soft rate limits; we can raise them for the POC if needed. Also, quotas are visible in the console.
[03:32] Nina: if we need Private, what's the timeline?
[03:36] Priya: Private deployments take longer — depends on packaging and networking, often 4–8 weeks for a standard on-cloud VPC deployment, on-prem can be longer. Dedicated is faster — a few days to weeks depending on commit.
[03:50] Tom: do you support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated?
[03:53] Priya: yes, customer KMS integrations are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports managed keys but we can discuss hybrid options.
[04:02] Marcus: any gotchas with model pins and rollouts? we need stable outputs for our user-facing features.
[04:07] Priya: we support model pinning and rollout policies—canary deploys, A/B tests, automatic fallbacks. Also quality monitoring so you can tie regressions to prompt sets/evals.
[04:20] Alicia: cost — how transparent is unit economics?
[04:23] Jordan: Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route and per-model dashboards, and optimizations from Redwood Optimize (caching, batching recommendations, quantization suggestions).
[04:38] Marcus: For the POC, can we run a real traffic replay?
[04:42] Priya: yes, we can replay recorded workload, run controlled latency/cost benchmarks. We'll need sample payloads and target SLAs.
[04:52] Jordan: sounds like a plan — we'll get you credits today, send the quickstart link, and Priya will set up the benchmark.
[04:59] Marcus: are there any common mis-steps?
[05:02] Priya: common is not accounting for prefix caching and batching in local tests — when you run at scale our runtime's KV cache and batching will change costs/latencies compared to a naive single-request test. We'll help you create a representative test.
[05:18] Nina: audit logs and retention? we need 12 months of audit trails for some product flows.
[05:23] Jordan: we have audit logs and retention policies; for Dedicated/Private you can control retention and where logs are stored. We'll include the specifics in the docs.
[05:34] Tom: how does billing for Dedicated look? commitment-based?
[05:37] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; it's priced for predictable throughput and lower per-token costs. We also have usage-based hosted pricing. We'll send ranges.
[05:50] Marcus: can you share a checklist for going from hosted to Dedicated?
[05:54] Priya: yes — we have a migration checklist: traffic profile, model versions, KV cache warmup, SLO targets, network config for VPC, KMS integration, and rollout plan. We'll attach it.
[06:08] Jordan: any competitors you're also looking at?
[06:11] Alicia: we've had evals with OpenAI and Anthropic, and some internal experiments with Hugging Face. Also checking AWS Bedrock for enterprise integration.
[06:20] Jordan: good to know. We'll highlight where Redwood's strengths are — production-grade runtime, cost controls, and unified experience across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[06:32] Marcus: ok, next steps? POC with latency/cost tests.
[06:36] Jordan: yep. I'll send the signup link and credits, Priya will reach out to schedule the POC. Nina, we'll also send SOC2 and KMS docs to you.
[06:45] Nina: thanks, please include SAML SSO details — we use Okta.
[06:49] Priya: okay, we support Okta via SAML; we'll share the SSO integration guide.
[06:55] Jordan: recap actions: (1) Jordan send quickstart + credits + pricing deck + SOC2 link. (2) Priya schedule bench. (3) Customer provide sample payloads and target SLOs.
[07:10] Alicia: sounds good, we aim to start POC early next week.
[07:14] Jordan: perfect, we'll follow up by end of day tomorrow. Thanks everyone.

[END]
